\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شوت} \fa{کردن} (shut kardan)}{شوت کردن (shut kardan)}]{\fa{شوت} \fa{کردن} (shut kardan) — to shoot (the ball)}

\label{lesson:FA-C515-shut-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a racket, then the Persian for a goalkeeper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شوت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{شوت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{shut kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to shoot (the ball)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{از} \fa{وسط} \fa{زمین} \fa{شوت} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u az vasat-e zamin shut kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He shot from the middle of the pitch.
\end{quote}

\emph{shut} 'a shot' + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shut} was borrowed from English \emph{shoot} (EtymDB). \emph{kardan}, 'to do', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shut kardan}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a racket, then the Persian for a goalkeeper, then say \emph{shut kardan} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پاس} \fa{دادن} (pâs dâdan)}{پاس دادن (pâs dâdan)}]{\fa{پاس} \fa{دادن} (pâs dâdan) — to pass (the ball)}

\label{lesson:FA-C515-pas-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a goalkeeper, then the Persian for to shoot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پاس} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{پاس} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{pâs dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to pass (the ball)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{توپ} \fa{را} \fa{به} \fa{دوستش} \fa{پاس} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u tup râ be dustash pâs dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He passed the ball to his friend.
\end{quote}

\emph{pâs} 'a pass' + \emph{dâdan} 'to give'; present stem \emph{deh-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pâs} was borrowed from English \emph{pass} (EtymDB). \emph{dâdan}, 'to give', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پرتاب} \fa{کردن} (partâb kardan)}{پرتاب کردن (partâb kardan)}]{\fa{پرتاب} \fa{کردن} (partâb kardan) — to hurl, to throw}

\label{lesson:FA-C515-partab-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to shoot, then the Persian for to pass.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پرتاب} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پرتاب} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{partâb kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to hurl, to throw\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{توپ} \fa{را} \fa{تا} \fa{آن} \fa{طرف} \fa{زمین} \fa{پرتاب} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u tup râ tâ ân taraf-e zamin partâb kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He threw the ball to the other end of the pitch.
\end{quote}

\emph{partâb} 'a throw' + \emph{kardan}. Stronger than \emph{andâkhtan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{partâb} is usually taken as a native Persian word for a throw, but EtymDB lists it without a source, and its origin is not settled. \emph{kardan} is inherited.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کشتی} \fa{گرفتن} (koshti gereftan)}{کشتی گرفتن (koshti gereftan)}]{\fa{کشتی} \fa{گرفتن} (koshti gereftan) — to wrestle}

\label{lesson:FA-C515-koshti-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to pass, then the Persian for to hurl.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کشتی} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{کشتی} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{koshti gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to wrestle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پسرها} \fa{در} \fa{باشگاه} \fa{کشتی} \fa{میگیرند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pesarhâ dar bâshgâh koshti migirand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boys wrestle at the club.
\end{quote}

\emph{koshti} 'wrestling' + \emph{gereftan}; present stem \emph{gir-}. Spelled like \emph{kashti} 'ship'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{koshti}, 'wrestling', is spelled like \emph{kashti}, 'ship', but is a different word, and no source used here gives its origin, which is not settled. \emph{gereftan} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{وزنه} \fa{برداری} (vazne bardâri)}{وزنه برداری (vazne bardâri)}]{\fa{وزنه} \fa{برداری} (vazne bardâri) — weightlifting}

\label{lesson:FA-C515-vazne-bardari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to hurl, then the Persian for to wrestle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{وزنه} \fa{برداری}}
\textbf{\fa{وزنه} \fa{برداری}} (\emph{vazne bardâri}) — \textquotedblleft{}weightlifting\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{هر} \fa{روز} \fa{وزنه} \fa{برداری} \fa{تمرین} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u har ruz vazne bardâri tamrin mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He practises weightlifting every day.
\end{quote}

\emph{vazne} 'a weight' + \emph{bardâri} 'lifting' (from \emph{bardâshtan}).

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vazne bardâri} is built in Persian on \emph{vazne}, 'a weight', from \emph{vazn}, a loan from Arabic \emph{wazn}, 'weight', and \emph{bardâri}, from native \emph{bardâshtan}, 'to lift'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
